full_text:
(1) This Act may be called the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023.
(2) It applies to all judicial proceedings in or before any Court, including Courts-martial, other than Courts-martial convened under the Army Act, 1950, the Navy Act, 1957 or the Air Force Act, 1950, but not to affidavits presented to any Court or officer, nor to proceedings before an arbitrator.
(3) It shall come into force on such date as the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint.

evidence_provision.rule_statement: Applies strictly to all judicial proceedings in or before any Court, excluding arbitration and standard affidavits
evidence_provision.statutory_condition: Must be a judicial proceeding before a competent court

evidence_provision.rule_statement: Comprehensive definitions establishing evidentiary standards: oral evidence, documentary evidence (including electronic and digital records), proved, disproved, and conclusive proof
evidence_provision.statutory_condition: Contextual baseline applicable across all provisions of the Adhiniyam
admissibility_criteria: Inclusion of digital records in documents

section_title: Confession to police officer not to be proved
full_text: No confession made to a police officer shall be proved as against a person accused of any offence.
chapter: PART II - CHAPTER II - RELEVANCY OF FACTS (ADMISSIONS & CONFESSIONS)

evidence_provision.rule_statement: Total exclusionary bar prohibiting proof of any confession made to a police officer as against an accused
evidence_provision.statutory_condition: Statement constitutes a confession and was made to a police officer
admissibility_criteria: Subject only to Section 23 discovery exception

section_title: How much of information received from accused may be proved (Discovery of Fact)
full_text: Provided that, when any fact is deposed to as discovered in consequence of information received from a person accused of any offence, in the custody of a police officer, so much of such information, whether it amounts to a confession or not, as relates distinctly to the fact thereby discovered, may be proved.
chapter: PART II - CHAPTER II - RELEVANCY OF FACTS (ADMISSIONS & CONFESSIONS)

evidence_provision.rule_statement: Statutory exception allowing proof of only that distinct portion of accused's statement in custody which directly led to the discovery of a relevant material fact or object
evidence_provision.statutory_condition: Accused was in police custody; information distinctly relates to and led directly to recovery of the fact/object
admissibility_criteria: Direct causal nexus between statement and discovery

full_text:
Primary evidence means the document itself produced for the inspection of the Court.
Explanation 1.-Where a document is executed in several parts, each part is primary evidence of the document.
Where a document is executed in counterpart, each counterpart being executed by one or some of the parties only, each counterpart is primary evidence as against the parties executing it.
Explanation 2.-Where a number of documents are all made by one uniform process, as in the case of printing, lithography, or photography, each is primary evidence of the contents of the rest; but, where they are all copies of a common original, they are not primary evidence of the contents of the original.
Explanation 3.-Where a document is created or stored in electronic form, including software or applications, each electronic store, memory or media shall be primary evidence.
chapter: PART III - CHAPTER V - OF DOCUMENTARY EVIDENCE

evidence_provision.rule_statement: Primary evidence is the original document itself produced for Court inspection; for electronic records, each store, memory, or media is primary evidence
evidence_provision.statutory_condition: Production of original document or native electronic storage media
admissibility_criteria: Native digital storage media qualifies as primary

section_title: Admissibility of electronic or digital record
full_text: Nothing in this Adhiniyam shall apply to deny the admissibility of an electronic or digital record, in the evidence on the ground that it is an electronic or digital record and such record shall have the same legal effect, validity and enforceability as other document, subject to section 63.
chapter: PART III - CHAPTER V - OF DOCUMENTARY EVIDENCE

evidence_provision.rule_statement: Digital records hold equal legal parity, validity, and enforceability with physical paper documents, subject to verification criteria under Section 63
evidence_provision.statutory_condition: Record is an electronic or digital record and complies with Section 63 authentication

section_title: Admissibility of electronic records and certificate requirement
full_text:
(1) Notwithstanding anything contained in this Adhiniyam, any information contained in an electronic record which is printed on a paper, stored, recorded or copied in optical or magnetic media produced by a computer shall be deemed to be also a document, if the conditions mentioned in this section are satisfied in relation to the information and computer in question and shall be admissible in any proceedings, without further proof or production of the original, as evidence of any contents of the original or of any fact stated therein of which direct evidence would be admissible.
(2) The conditions referred to in sub-section (1) in respect of a computer output shall be the following:-(a) the computer output containing the information was produced by the computer during the period over which the computer was used regularly to store or process information; (b) during the said period, information of the kind contained in the electronic record was regularly fed into the computer in the ordinary course of the said activities; (c) throughout the material part of the said period, the computer was operating properly; (d) the information contained in the electronic record reproduces or is derived from such information fed into the computer in the ordinary course of the said activities.
(4) In any proceeding where it is desired to give a statement in evidence by virtue of this section, a certificate doing any of the following things shall be produced, namely:-(a) identifying the electronic record containing the statement and describing the manner in which it was produced; (b) giving such particulars of any device involved in the production of that electronic record; (c) signed by a person in charge of the computer or management of the relevant activities.
chapter: PART III - CHAPTER V - OF DOCUMENTARY EVIDENCE

evidence_provision.rule_statement: Mandatory statutory conditions and certificate requirement for admissibility of secondary computer outputs, printouts, and digital storage media
evidence_provision.statutory_condition: Regular course of computer operation and valid Certificate signed by person in management/charge of system (Schedule / Section 63(4))
admissibility_criteria: Regular computer operation during material period

chapter: PART IV - CHAPTER XI - REPEAL AND SAVINGS

evidence_provision.rule_statement: Repeals the Indian Evidence Act 1872 while preserving evidentiary status of proceedings instituted prior to commencement
evidence_provision.statutory_condition: Proceedings commenced prior to date of repeal
admissibility_criteria: Preservation of past evidence and accrued rights under IEA 1872
